title: I Logged Every Carpool Detour My Brother Called a Shortcut

parts.text: I picked Evan up at 7:22 a.m. and he asked if we could swing by the gym, the dry cleaner, and a drive-through because it was on the way. It was not on the way. I was thirty-three, paying for the Civic and the downtown garage. He called every extra light a shortcut. I started a notes app: time, odometer, stop, his quote. By Thursday the log had eleven stops and a smoothie he did not offer to split. Friday he said I was being weird about family. I screenshotted the log and texted, still in the garage queue. Then his manager called him because he was eleven minutes late to a standup he blamed on my driving.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: His standup is late and the log shows the smoothie stop, not my route.

social.description: Civic, garage, eleven extra stops. He blamed my driving. Would you have sent the log?

parts.text: I sent Evan the log and a Venmo for gas using IRS mileage, which is a love language. He paid half and started taking the train two days a week. I still pick him up when the route is the route. The notes app is archived, not deleted. Family is not a rideshare without a pin. The Civic smells like rain instead of blended mango. His standup is on time when he is.
